s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of dizziness, vertigo, and altered mental status with intermittent focal neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Episodes of prominent dizziness, vertigo, and dull response
Recurrent episodes more than 10 times a day, each lasting about 5 minutes
Rhythmic epileptiform discharges on EEG originating from the right frontal area
key_facts: 67-year-old male with hypertension and coronary artery disease
Presented with episodes of dizziness, vertigo, and left arm shaking
Episodes occurred while playing Mah-Jong
Patient was partially aware during episodes but unable to think
Each episode lasted about 5 minutes
Episodes recurred more than 10 times a day
Blood pressure was 200/110 mmHg at triage
Neurological examination was unremarkable except for dull response during events
No focal brainstem signs, left-right disorientation, dyslexia, dysgraphia, or finger agnosia
Basic laboratory data were within normal limits
Brain MRI revealed non-specific white matter changes
EEG showed rhythmic epileptiform discharges from the right frontal area

shortlist.label: Frontal lobe epilepsy
shortlist.why_kept: EEG showed rhythmic epileptiform discharges from the right frontal area

shortlist.label: Temporal lobe epilepsy
shortlist.why_kept: Episodes of altered mental status and focal neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Gelastic epilepsy
shortlist.why_kept: Episodes of dizziness, vertigo, and altered mental status with possible gelastic seizures

shortlist.label: Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of focal seizures and altered mental status

shortlist.label: Cavernous angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of focal seizures and altered mental status due to vascular malformation

raw.rationale: The patient's episodes of dizziness, vertigo, and left arm shaking, along with the EEG findings of rhythmic epileptiform discharges originating from the right frontal area, support the diagnosis of frontal lobe epilepsy.

rejected.label: Temporal lobe epilepsy
rejected.why: The EEG findings do not indicate involvement of the temporal lobe.

rejected.label: Gelastic epilepsy
rejected.why: The patient's episodes do not involve laughter or humorous feelings, which are characteristic of gelastic epilepsy.

rejected.label: Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor
rejected.why: There is no evidence of a tumor on the brain MRI, which only showed non-specific white matter changes.

rejected.label: Cavernous angioma
rejected.why: There is no evidence of a vascular malformation on the brain MRI, which would be expected in cavernous angioma.
